 Food Components Th e role of 
several other nutrients and food components in the prevention 
of osteoporosis has been studied. Among these are phosphorus, 
protein, fruits and vegetables, sodium, caﬀ eine, ﬂ uoride, and 
trace minerals. Phosphorus is an essential bone-forming miner-
al, and an adequate supply is necessary for optimal bone health
throughout life. According to data from NHANES 1999–2000,
mean intakes of phosphorus are well above the RDAs for both 
sexes at all age levels except for males 6 to 11 years of age and
females 9 to 18 years of age. In these two groups, mean intakes 
are slightly less than the RDA. Apart from these two age cate-
gories, it appears that the phosphorus intakes of Americans are 
adequate except for instances of malnutrition, intestinal malab-
sorption, and excessive use of phosphorus-binding antacids.18, 22
Concerns have been raised about diets high in phosphorus and
low in calcium resulting in a high phosphorus:calcium ratio, 
particularly in relation to the consumption of carbonated soft-
drinks. Th e ratio of phosphorus to calcium in the diet can vary 
widely with no detectable eﬀ ect on the absorption and reten-
tion of either mineral or on BMD. Phosphorus-rich carbonated
soft-drinks appear to only have a negligible eﬀ ect on calcium 
excretion.18, 22
